name: Atlas AI Store Builder
summary: Shopify app that builds a full store or product page from a single product link, with layout, copy and images generated automatically, plus bundle and cart upsells.
best_for: sellers testing many product ideas quickly who want a full Shopify storefront from a single product link, and who will stay inside 10 pages and 250 orders a month or have priced the overage
skip_if: you run one established store with real order volume, the caps turn a $39 tool into a variable bill exactly when the store starts working, or you want a page builder you keep after you stop paying
honest_knock: The meter runs on your success, not your usage. $1,000 of bundle revenue and 250 cart orders is a rounding error for a store that is actually working. So the $39 headline describes the bill of a store that has not started selling yet. Price the tier you expect to be on in month three, not the one you sign up on. Two other things worth knowing before you install. The record stands at 374 reviews on 9 October 2026, but 25 of those are one star and the recent ones are about billing rather than the product: one seller writes “cancelled it, uninstalled it, but still getting charged” after two months. And the listing carries a line Shopify does not require of most apps: “Atlas must not be used to copy, duplicate, or reproduce products, product listings, images, or store content from any website, or marketplace without the explicit permission of the rights holder”. That tells you what a paste-a-product-link builder gets used for.

pricing.entry_price_terms: All-in-one · per month, plus usage charges that scale with the revenue your store generates -- the vendor does not publish that rate
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-09 on apps.shopify.com/dropshipt and helloatlas.io; first read 2026-08-18) The listing says “Free to install”, but that is the development-store tier. A real store runs on the All-in-One plan at $39 a month, billed in USD with a 7-day free trial. What $39 buys is capped rather than unlimited. On 9 October 2026 the vendor's pricing section lists up to 10 published pages (it was 5 on 18 August), up to $1,000 of bundle revenue and up to 250 cart orders; AI photos, listed at 50 in August, no longer appear in that list. Their pricing page states it plainly: “you’ll be charged the base plan fees and given access to features to a limit, any additional uses for those features can be purchased as shown in the per feature pricing”, but the rendered page showed no per-feature prices on 9 October. The App Store listing adds that “additional charges apply as your store generates revenue and impact”, and that recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Atlas AI Store Builder on a Shopify development store: the install with no payment screen, one AI product page for Demo Mug made in about 1.5 minutes and 9 clicks and saved as a draft, with invented placeholder social proof in the preview (10,000+ and 438 people purchased) and a sample review, then Upgrade to generate and Upgrade to publish everywhere. The Subscription page showed the $39 plan with a 7-day trial and the limits as the dossier says, and a dialog with the usage rates; Start 7-day free trial kept spinning and led to a login page of the vendor, so the Shopify approval screen was not reached and nothing was approved. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the App Store listing (English) was used and the install form was submitted in our own tab at 18:41; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked. There was no plan choice and no payment screen at the install. The app opened directly on Create with Atlas AI with three choices (Store, Product pages, Landing pages); the sidebar of the app had Your Pages, Bundle Deals, Cart Upsells and Subscription. No password, card, phone number or sign-up form of the vendor was asked. The admin was in English. Core action, one AI product page for the product Demo Mug: Product pages, Demo Mug ticked (1 product selected), Continue setup, the template Atlas Default (Universal) (Used by 174,553 stores), Continue setup, Upload research (Optional) skipped, Continue setup, then Researching your product... and Writing your page.... The result stood there at 18:43, about 1 minute 30 seconds after the install and 9 clicks. The editor showed the page of Demo Mug with $9.50, four labels, 10,000+ next to the stars, the line Sarah and 438 people purchased, a sample review card that says This is a sample review, please input your genuine customer review and 25 in stock. The store had no such numbers: they are invented placeholder social proof in the preview, recorded here as an observation. The buttons were Save as draft and Upgrade to publish; Save as draft was clicked and nothing was published. After that every generate button on the home page of the app said Upgrade to generate (Full store, Product page and so on) and the setup guide said 1 out of 4 steps completed. Plans in the app: the Subscription page showed the Atlas base plan, $39 per month, All features included, only pay more as your business grows, with a button Start 7-day free trial. Included: published product and landing pages up to 10, bundle revenue up to $1,000, cart orders up to 250. The text says that if the usage is exceeded, the usage rates are charged. Usage rates (read in the app, they answer the open dossier question about them): published pages, Base up to 10 included, up to 15 +$10 a month, up to 25 +$20, up to 50 +$30, up to 75 +$40, up to 100 +$50, unlimited +$70; bundler, Base up to $1,000 included, up to $2,500 +$10, up to $5,000 +$20, up to $10,000 +$35, up to $20,000 +$65, up to $35,000 +$110, up to $50,000 +$150 and above $50,000 +$195 a month. The tab Cart drawer could not be read because the click was not processed. Difference with the dossier: the dossier says the rendered pricing page showed no per-feature prices on 9 October; the app shows the usage rates in a dialog, so that line is out of date for the app. The $39 plan, the 7-day trial and the limits (10 pages, $1,000, 250 orders) are as the dossier says. Checkout: NOT reached. Start 7-day free trial was clicked; the button kept spinning for more than 20 seconds and the Shopify screen Approve subscription did not appear. A next click (closing the rates dialog) sent the tab to the login page of the vendor (app.helloatlas.io/api/auth), which only said Enter your shop domain to log in or install this app.; nothing was entered. No test charge was seen, nothing was approved, no card was entered and nothing was paid. The app home was blank several times (about 30 seconds, directly by address and from the sidebar) and loaded after a detour. Cancelling: no plan was started, so a stop of the billing could not be tested. The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu of Atlas, Uninstall; the dialog says that after uninstalling any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; a reason for uninstalling is required before the button works. Not tested: publishing (it needs an upgrade), bundles, cart upsells, Store and Landing pages, the trial approval screen, the Cart drawer tab of the rates and whether billing stops after the uninstall. Clean up: before the uninstall no new page was found under Online Store, Pages (5 existing pages, none from Atlas) and no new theme was found (the live theme and two drafts were older); the draft stays in the app, not in Shopify; the app embeds in the theme were not checked. Atlas was uninstalled after the test in our own tab and our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: After the first draft every generate and publish button said Upgrade; the generated preview carried invented numbers (10,000+, 438 people purchased) and a sample review the merchant has to replace; Start 7-day free trial kept spinning and ended on a login page of the vendor; the app home was blank several times for about 30 seconds; and the uninstall asked for a reason before it worked.

Publishing a page, bundles, cart upsells, and the Store and Landing pages options.
